routes.description: Establish that theistic idealism provides a more plausible unified explanation than naturalism for consciousness, emergent physical reality, objective morality, and the ultimate cosmological foundation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if mind is shown to be irreducible and explanatorily fundamental, the disputed phenomena support a necessary personal ground, and one unlimited mind explains the total evidence with greater comparative economy than the naturalistic alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect the combined evidence from consciousness, emergence, morality, and cosmology to the conclusion that theism is more plausible than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Show that conscious experience is not reducible to physical computation and that physical reality can coherently be understood as emergent from mind.
Show that the informational, relational, quantum, and structurally mind-like features of the universe support a mental rather than self-sufficient material foundation.
Show that contingent minds and objective personal moral obligations require a necessary and perfect personal ground.
Show that one unlimited mind explains the debated domains with fewer independent brute commitments than the naturalistic cosmological and reductive alternatives.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish that the proposed lawless or minimally specified natural origin lacks an adequate causal and probabilistic basis for producing the observed universe.
Defend the claim that an unlimited partless mind can be ontologically simple despite possessing maximal knowledge, power, and explanatory scope.

routes.description: Establish that secular naturalism is more plausible because physical and evolutionary mechanisms explain the disputed evidence, while a minimally specified natural origin is simpler and predicts the observed world better than a perfect divine mind.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the detailed evidence concerning brains, cosmic structure, moral development, and natural causal precedent is more expected under naturalism, and if theistic unification depends on unsupported reductions or a highly specified divine posit.

motionBridge.description: Connect naturalistic explanations and likelihood comparisons across all four evidential domains to the conclusion that theism is not more plausible than naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Show through computational modeling, neural intervention, comparative anatomy, and evolution that consciousness depends causally on physical brain systems.
Explain cosmic and neural structural similarities through ordinary physical organization rather than treating them as evidence of universe-scale mentality.
Ground moral imperatives without a divine person and show that gradual, error-prone moral development is expected under naturalism.
Show that a minimally specified random origin or sparse brute foundation is simpler than an omniscient, omnipotent, and morally perfect mind.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Apply parsimony, established causal precedent, and comparative evidential likelihood to the complete set of disputed phenomena.
Explain why privileged first-person access to an instantiated computation does not prevent third-person neural evidence from supporting physicalism.

sections.title: Consciousness, Computation, and Physical Reduction
sections.rationale: Whether subjective experience is irreducible or instead caused by computational brain systems determines the foundational contrast between idealism and physicalism and bears directly on which worldview predicts embodied consciousness.

sections.title: Emergence, Information, and Cosmic Structure
sections.rationale: The competing interpretations of fundamental physics, quantum cognition, and cosmic-neural resemblance determine whether emergent physical reality supplies positive evidence for a mind-like foundation or ordinary physical organization.

sections.title: Morality, Obligation, and Historical Development
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether objective obligations require a transcendent personal source or can arise as empirically grounded overriding imperatives, including which account better anticipates the observed development of moral practice.

sections.title: Cosmological Origins, Probability, and Brute Facts
sections.rationale: The coherence and generative adequacy of a lawless or minimally specified origin are central to whether naturalism offers a genuine cosmological alternative and whether its brute commitments are preferable to a necessary mind.

sections.title: Parsimony, Prediction, and Explanatory Unification
sections.rationale: The motion ultimately requires comparing the total explanatory scope, prior plausibility, predictive fit, and ontological commitments of one unlimited divine mind with the naturalistic accounts offered across all four evidential domains.
